steps.title: Open the Desk page
steps.narration: The Desk is your intraday setup scanner. It loads with the Playbook Signals section, ready to analyze recorded trading sessions.
steps.point_out: The Playbook Signals panel is visible with a date input field and a Run Playbook button.

steps.title: Enter a session date
steps.narration: The Playbook analyzes one trading session at a time. We'll examine a session from June 22, 2026, which fired all three new setup types.
steps.point_out: The date field now contains the session date.

steps.title: Run the Playbook
steps.narration: Click to scan the session for signals. The Playbook detects setup patterns using the pre-registered rules in the specification.
steps.point_out: The button shows Computing… briefly, then returns to Run Playbook with a completion message.

steps.title: View the signals table with new setup types
steps.narration: The table displays every setup detected in the session. You now see three new setup types — Jump-Base Explosion, Drop-Base Implosion, and Cup and Handle — each with its own chip label in the setup column.
steps.point_out: The signals table shows rows for LADDER (Jump-Base Explosion), DBI1 (Drop-Base Implosion), and CUP1 (Cup and Handle) with distinct setup chips.

steps.title: Expand a Jump-Base Explosion signal
steps.narration: JBE shows a tight consolidation base followed by a sharp upside move. Click the row to see the base width in MBR, the jump size, and the bar where it broke.
steps.point_out: The detail panel expands, showing the JBE-specific geometry line: base width, bar count, jump size, breakout slot, and base quality notes.

steps.title: Expand a Drop-Base Implosion signal
steps.narration: DBI is the short-side mirror of JBE. The same geometry fields show base and jump magnitudes, direction-flipped for a downside move.
steps.point_out: The detail panel shows the DBI geometry line with base width, bar count, jump size for the short side.

steps.title: Expand a Cup and Handle signal
steps.narration: Cup and Handle shows a different geometry: a rounded cup pullback, then a smaller handle retrace, then a breakout. The disclosure includes cup bar count, depth in MBR, handle retrace and duration fractions, and three relative volume medians.
steps.point_out: The detail panel displays Cup and Handle geometry: cup bars and depth, handle retrace fraction, handle duration, and the three RVOL medians describing volume distribution.
